findings.title: Travellers get permanently blue visited countries after a temporary flag-service failure — failures and fallback tiles are cached as successes
findings.observed: Third-party integrations: source prediction, not an executed provider failure. If the flag request times out or is rejected on its first request for a visited country, None is retained in the process cache and every later render for that country uses flat cyan, even after the provider recovers. The generated fallback tile is also cached server-side and for a week in browsers. Travellers cannot restore their promised flag colours by ordinary refresh or re-adding the visit; the country remains recorded and other travel-log tasks remain available.
findings.evidence: backend/tiles.py:49-56 decorates _flag with @lru_cache(maxsize=256) and returns None on any exception; :66-67 caches render_tile; :89-92 substitutes the solid colour (0,180,216) for None. backend/server.py:228 serves the result with 'public, max-age=604800'.
findings.expected: R-009: "never turning into ... a flat blue block"; checklist, Third-party integrations: "Follow unavailable, rejected, partial, delayed ... dependency outcomes to visible status and recovery." A transient failure should be indicated/retryable rather than permanently cached as the final flag fill.
reproduction_steps: With Italy visited, open Mi Mundo in a backend process that has not yet loaded Italy's flag.
Condition: the initial flag-provider request fails or times out.
After the provider recovers, reload and zoom into Italy again: the cached None still selects solid cyan, and existing fallback tiles retain their long-lived success cache.

findings.title: Failed attachment uploads leave country saves stuck and city/trip retries duplicated — dialogs recreate already committed parents instead of resuming uploads
findings.surface: Añadir país visitado; Añadir ciudad; Nuevo viaje with attachments
findings.observed: UI state, navigation and interaction: source prediction. Choose Gibraltar with a valid date and an image larger than 25 MiB (or encounter a storage/network failure). The visit is durably saved, but the dialog reports failure, does not refresh the globe/list/passport, and retains creation mode. Replacing the rejected photo and pressing Save again only produces 'Ya tienes este país registrado'. The analogous city/trip dialogs are worse: the retry creates a second city/trip, because they have no uniqueness guard or retained operation id. A city retry produces two same-position globe labels for one save intent and duplicate visit records. Recovery requires abandoning/reloading and editing or deleting partially created records; existing records/photos are not proven lost.
findings.evidence: AddCountryDialog.jsx:32-36 POSTs /visited before uploading; :38-42 only refreshes/closes after every step succeeds. server.py:292-294 refuses a later create for that country with 409. AddCityDialog.jsx:41-47 likewise POSTs /cities then uploads, and TripDialog.jsx:32-41 creates the trip then uploads its cover. Neither retains the created id on failure. server.py:502-504 and :394-396 create a new UUID/record on each city/trip retry; :606-607 rejects oversized images after the parent already exists.
findings.expected: R-003: "saving marks Gibraltar as visited on screen without a reload"; request: "Añadir una fotografía ... Guardar el país como visitado" and "Subir fotografías ... Guardarla" for cities; checklist, UI state, navigation and interaction: "Trace ... cancellation, partial failure and the final communicated result" and "one create ... per intent." A failed attachment must preserve a recoverable saved parent and let the user retry the attachment, not retry creation.
reproduction_steps: In Mi Mundo → Añadir país visitado, select Gibraltar, enter a date and select an image exceeding 25 MiB.
Press Guardar como visitado, then replace the rejected image and retry: the durable visit makes the creation retry fail as already registered.
Separately, use Añadir ciudad for Roma with an oversized attachment; after its upload rejection, replace the file and press Guardar ciudad again.
Reload Mis ciudades/Mi Mundo: the first failed-looking attempt and retry have created two Roma records/labels. Nuevo viaje with a failed cover upload has the same duplicate-parent retry pattern.

findings.title: Visited French territories stay grey at close zoom and France colours them instead — tile geometry uses FR for independently selectable territory codes
findings.surface: Mi Mundo globe; GET /api/tiles/{z}/{x}/{y}.jpg?v=RE (also YT, GP, MQ, GF)
findings.observed: Data, persistence and APIs: source prediction. A traveller saves Réunion without France, then zooms in. The tile renderer never matches RE, and the pin is also removed at altitude <0.9, so Réunion stays unvisited grey. Conversely, visiting France alone colours Réunion even though its separate visit record is absent. The same mismatch affects five newly supported territories. List/passport recording remains available, but the globe misrepresents which places were visited.
findings.evidence: backend/countries_data.py:237-242 defines GP, MQ, GF, RE, YT as independently visitable territories. backend/data/countries50.geojson:1 contains no features with these codes: their polygons belong to code FR (e.g. Réunion bounds 55.232813,-21.369043 to 55.839063,-20.865137). backend/tiles.py:35 stores that feature code and :82-83 skips its fill unless that code is visited. WorldGlobe.jsx:49 returns only cities at close zoom, removing the territory flag pins used at world view.
findings.expected: R-010: "fills the visited countries inside their borders ... leaves unvisited countries dark"; request: "Cuando un usuario marque un país como visitado, ese país cambiará de color." checklist, Data, persistence and APIs: "map source value → normalized representation → user/API option → effective predicate." Independently selectable RE/YT/GP/MQ/GF must reach their own geometry or retain a truthful flag-pin fallback at close zoom.
reproduction_steps: In Mi Mundo, add Reunión as visited but do not mark Francia.
Zoom into Réunion below altitude 0.9: no RE geometry can be filled and its flag pin disappears.
Alternatively mark only Francia and inspect Réunion: its FR-coded polygon receives the France visit fill despite RE remaining unvisited.

findings.title: Travellers cannot reach photos beyond the first 200 in a city gallery — the list is silently capped and has no pagination
findings.observed: Files, media and generated artifacts: source prediction. A traveller who accumulates 201 valid photos in a city can see the full count but only view/edit/delete/reorder the first 200; there is no ordinary UI route to the remaining photo. Files remain in storage, so this is bounded loss of access, not proven deletion. A trip gallery has the same default cap; public city/trip shares separately cap at 500.
findings.evidence: backend/server.py:648 defaults limit to 200 (maximum 1000), :656 uses to_list(limit) without offset/cursor/total. PhotoGallery.jsx:39 calls /photos with only city_id/trip_id and :45 renders only that response; :95-111 has no next-page or load-more action. backend/server.py:469 counts all gallery photos, so the city header can show more files than the gallery can access.
findings.expected: request: "Quiero poder subir tantas fotografías como quiera" and "Abrir fotografías a pantalla completa ... Eliminar fotografías ... Editar descripciones ... Ordenar fotografías"; checklist, Data, persistence and APIs: "Check pagination reaches the last page ... exposes truncation." All saved photos need a reachable page/load-more path with truthful counts.
reproduction_steps: Add a city and upload 201 valid photos in batches of at most 50.
Open that city's page: its Galería count includes all 201.
Inspect the grid and full-screen navigation: only 200 photos are returned, with no continuation to the final one.

findings.title: Selecting more than 50 photos silently drops the rest — upload processes a sliced batch and returns success
findings.observed: Files, media and generated artifacts: source prediction. On selecting 51 valid photos, the server stores only the first 50, silently discards the 51st from processing and returns success. The UI clears the selection and gives no rejected/skipped-file explanation. The traveller must notice the count mismatch and reselect missing files; originals are not deleted, so recovery is possible but the requested batch is not completed.
findings.evidence: backend/server.py:634 loops 'for i, f in enumerate(files[:50])' then :637 returns out as a normal success without reporting omitted files. frontend/src/lib/api.js:45 submits every selected file; PhotoGallery.jsx:51-56 toasts the returned count and clears the file input.
findings.expected: request: "Subir varias fotografías simultáneamente" and "subir tantas fotografías como quiera"; checklist, Files, media and generated artifacts: "visible rejected/skipped input" and "a configuration batch applying half its entries must not report complete success." Process the batch, explicitly reject an over-limit batch before writes, or return clear per-file omissions that can be retried.
reproduction_steps: Open a city's Galería and choose Subir fotografías.
Select 51 valid small JPEG files in one selection.
The request contains 51 files, but the success response and saved collection contain only the first 50, with no explicit warning about the skipped file.

findings.title: Travellers' distinct same-named cities are counted as one — city identity discards coordinates and administrative region
findings.surface: Mi Mundo city statistic; Mis estadísticas; visited-country cities_count
findings.observed: Business logic and calculations: source prediction. A traveller selects two different same-named cities in the same country from the worldwide search. Both records and coordinate labels survive, but the profile/world statistics and country cards count only one city; the most-visited-city grouping can also turn the two distinct places into two visits to a single city. Users can still open both records, but cannot obtain accurate city statistics without changing real place names.
findings.evidence: backend/stats.py:65 defines unique_cities as {(c['name'].strip().lower(), c['country_code']) for c in cities}; :103 derives n_cities from that set; :97 similarly groups repeat visits by name/country. backend/server.py:264-266 counts cities per country using only $toLower:'$name'. CityIn (server.py:437-440) and world search (server.py:243-244) retain distinct coordinates and admin1, but neither count uses them.
findings.expected: request: "Número de ciudades visitadas" and "Las ciudades tendrán sus propias estadísticas independientes"; checklist, Data, persistence and APIs: "Establish logical record ... identity ... a distinct similar item that must remain separate." Identity inference: two different municipalities in different administrative regions/coordinates are different cities even when their labels and ISO country match; visiting Springfield, Illinois and Springfield, Massachusetts means two cities, not one.
reproduction_steps: Use Añadir ciudad to select Springfield in Illinois, United States.
Add a second Springfield in Massachusetts, United States, selecting its different geocoding result.
Open Mi Mundo and the United States country entry: the distinct saved cities contribute only 1 to the unique-city counts.

findings.title: A rejected city-search request looks like 'no matching city' and loses globe positioning — upstream HTTP errors are not checked
findings.observed: Third-party integrations: source prediction conditional on an upstream JSON error such as a rate-limit response without 'results'. HTTP rejection is converted to 200 [] by this handler, so travellers are told to add their real city manually rather than that search failed. Manual entries have null coordinates and cannot appear in the newly requested globe label layer. Users may retry later, but the false empty success gives no reason to do so and existing manual cities have no coordinate editor.
findings.evidence: backend/server.py:238 awaits the upstream GET but never calls raise_for_status(); :239 takes r.json().get('results') or []; :243-245 returns that as normal results. CitySearch.jsx:21 sets the returned array, :22 only shows an error on rejected requests, and :45-48 presents manual entry on empty successful results.
findings.expected: request: "Buscador mundial de ciudades"; R-012: "Every city saved through the world city search stores its latitude and longitude"; checklist, Third-party integrations: "Follow unavailable, rejected, partial ... dependency outcomes to visible status and recovery." A rejected geocoder request must be distinguished from a genuine empty search, with a visible retryable failure.
reproduction_steps: Open Añadir ciudad and type a known city such as Roma.
Condition: the geocoder replies with a non-2xx JSON error object rather than results.
The API returns [] successfully; the UI offers Añadir «Roma» manualmente without showing its search-service failure message.
If saved manually, the city has null coordinates and is omitted from the globe.

findings.title: Keyboard gallery users tab through the hidden page instead of the full-screen editor — Lightbox never manages modal focus or background interaction
findings.observed: Layout, theme, visuals and UX: source prediction, not a measured layout. Keyboard users opening a gallery photo retain focus on the obscured underlying grid button. Tab traverses the remaining page and gallery instead of entering/remaining in the overlay; background links can still be activated while the full-screen layer is visible. With many photos this creates substantial navigation work to reach the overlay's own Close/editor controls, and can navigate away from an editing session. Escape/arrow hotkeys help outside fields but do not establish the missing focus contract.
findings.evidence: Lightbox.jsx:8-17 installs only a window keydown listener (and skips INPUT/TEXTAREA/SELECT entirely at :10). :20 renders a fixed div without dialog semantics, focus assignment/trapping or background inert/scroll locking. PhotoGallery.jsx:98 opens it from a grid button and :115 mounts it after that grid; none of these paths move focus.
findings.expected: checklist, Layout, theme, visuals and UX: "keyboard focus stays visible and follows the active surface" and "an editor overlay must preserve the supported focus/background interaction contract." Opening full-screen media should move keyboard focus into the overlay, contain it there, and restore focus on closing.
reproduction_steps: Use Tab to focus an early photo in a city gallery containing many photos, and press Enter.
Press Tab: focus remains in the background document's order rather than being moved to the full-screen Close control.
Continue tabbing or activate an underlying link while the full-screen overlay remains visible; focus is neither trapped nor restored by the component.

findings.title: API users can save a city's end before its start with a partial edit — date validation ignores the stored counterpart
findings.observed: Business logic and calculations: source prediction. For an owned city with visit_date=2026-06-10 and end_date=2026-06-12, an API caller updating only end_date to 2026-06-01 passes validation and persists a backwards range. The city page then displays the contradictory saved dates. The owner can repair the dates with another edit; the supported modular API cannot rely on the full-body browser form to enforce its state rule.
findings.evidence: server.py:525 fetches the existing city but :527 only compares data.get('visit_date') and data.get('end_date') from the request. :541 stores the partial data without comparing the merged dates. CityUpdate :452-453 declares both dates optional; the API contract permits partial PUT bodies.
findings.expected: checklist, Business logic and calculations: "Trace each rule on create/edit ... including server validation"; checklist, Data, persistence and APIs: "partial updates preserve omitted fields." The existing invariant explicitly enforced at server.py:494-495/:527-528 is 'La fecha final es anterior a la inicial': a partial edit must validate that invariant against the resulting record, not just fields included together.
reproduction_steps: Save an owned city with Desde 2026-06-10 and Hasta 2026-06-12.
As its signed-in owner, use the documented PUT /api/cities/{id} operation with only end_date='2026-06-01'.
GET the city: the request has succeeded and now returns end_date earlier than the preserved visit_date.

findings.title: A rejected city edit still moves its photos into another trip — dependent writes happen before cover validation
findings.surface: PUT /api/cities/{city_id}; trip galleries and shared trip gallery
findings.observed: Data, persistence and APIs: source prediction. An owner uses the supported city-update API to change a city's trip and cover together, but supplies an unavailable cover id. The response says 404 while the city still belongs to its original trip and its gallery photos now belong to the new trip. The old trip loses those images from its photo listing, and the new trip gains them despite the failed save. If that new trip is individually shared, its public photo listing also gains the moved images. Repair requires manually reconciling the city/trip linkage; no rollback or explanation is returned.
findings.evidence: server.py:529-534 updates the new trip's country_codes and every city photo's trip_id before :535-537 validates cover_photo_id. If that photo is missing or not owned, :537 raises HTTPException(404), and the city's own trip_id is never committed at :541. list_photos at :654-656 reads the already-changed photo trip_id, whereas get_city at :517-519 reads the unchanged city trip_id.
findings.expected: checklist, Data, persistence and APIs: "Multi-document operations leave no half-written state on failure"; checklist, UI state, navigation and interaction: "failed transitions preserve or explain remaining valid state." A rejected city update must not move its photos into another trip or alter the target trip's countries.
reproduction_steps: Create trips A and B, and a city in A with at least one gallery photo.
As the city owner, PUT /api/cities/{id} with trip_id=B and an unavailable cover_photo_id.
Observe the 404 response.
Read the city and the two trips' photo listings: the city remains in A while its photos are now assigned to B.

findings.title: Accepted iPhone HEIC photos cannot be viewed by Android travellers — original HEIC bytes are served without a browser-compatible derivative
findings.surface: Photo upload; city/trip/shared galleries and Lightbox
findings.observed: Files, media and generated artifacts: source prediction for a valid original HEIC/HEIF file supplied to the accepted upload API. The upload is reported successful and increases photo counts, but an Android/Chrome viewer that cannot decode HEIC receives only the original HEIC image in its grid and lightbox, so sees a broken image instead of the travel photo. The same image can fail for friends on shared links. This is recoverable by externally converting and reuploading, but no conversion/replacement recovery is offered in the app.
findings.evidence: server.py:581 explicitly allows image/heic and image/heif. :605 reads original data; :610 uploads those unmodified bytes; :611 stores the same content_type. :711-714 retrieves and serves those original bytes. PhotoGallery.jsx:99-101 and Lightbox.jsx:26-28 render all non-video media directly with ; there is no conversion or alternate browser-compatible image.
findings.expected: request: "Las fotografías deben poder subirse y visualizarse" and "El diseño debe funcionar correctamente en Android, iPhone, tablet y ordenador"; checklist, Files, media and generated artifacts: "output usable under the promised format." Accepted phone photo formats need a browser-compatible derivative (with the original preserved if desired), or a clear rejection before claiming successful publication.
reproduction_steps: Upload an original valid image/heic photo to a city (using a picker/client that supplies the original rather than converting it to JPEG).
Open that city gallery or its Compartir galería link in Android Chrome, which does not decode HEIC in .
The saved photo URL returns the original HEIC bytes; neither the grid nor full-screen view has a compatible derivative.

findings.title: Clicking Gibraltar's coloured area opens Spain instead — high-detail tiles and click targets use different country geometries
findings.surface: Mi Mundo globe → country click → country-info-dialog
findings.observed: UI state, navigation and interaction: source prediction, supported by calculation against both supplied geometry files, not a browser click observation. After saving Gibraltar and zooming close, its tile can be coloured correctly but clicking its visible territory dispatches ES and opens Spain's record/actions. Vatican City and San Marino similarly resolve to Italy. The correct country remains accessible from Mis países, so this is a recoverable navigation failure rather than loss of the visit.
findings.evidence: WorldGlobe.jsx:7 loads frontend/public/countries.geojson and :83-90 uses those features exclusively for country click identity. That source (line 1) has 177 features and no GI, VA or SM, while backend/data/countries50.geojson:1 has separate GI/VA/SM used by tiles.py:24-35. A read-only point-in-polygon calculation on the supplied coordinates places lng=-5.35,lat=36.125 inside backend GI but frontend ES (and lng=12.433,lat=41.901 inside backend VA but frontend IT). WorldGlobe.jsx:49 removes flag-pin click targets at close zoom. MiMundo.jsx:57-59 opens/focuses the code supplied by that stale polygon, so clicking ES opens Spain.
findings.expected: request: "Al pulsar sobre un país se abrirá una ventana con su información" and "No esta en la lista el pais de Gibraltar"; checklist, UI state, navigation and interaction: "follow ... identifiers ... to the destination, object, content and permitted actions it promises." The displayed territory and its click target must have the same identity, including at the newly supported close zoom.
reproduction_steps: Save Gibraltar in Mi Mundo and zoom close to it, below altitude 0.9 where the flag pin is removed.
Click the rendered Gibraltar area around latitude 36.125, longitude -5.35.
The active frontend polygon is ES, so the info window identifies/focuses Spain instead of Gibraltar.
Repeat at the separately coloured Vatican City area: the frontend hit geometry identifies Italy.

findings.title: Experienced travellers wait tens of seconds for cold globe tiles — each intersecting country's flag is downloaded serially before a tile can respond
findings.surface: Mi Mundo world-view tiles; GET /api/tiles/2/2/1.jpg?v=<visited codes>
findings.observed: Performance and resource leaks: source-derived latency estimate, not measured latency. On a fresh worker/cache, a traveller with 20 visited countries intersecting this ordinary world-view tile blocks its response on 20 serial flag downloads plus the imagery request. If each otherwise successful flag download takes one second, the tile cannot finish in less than roughly 20 seconds; a 20-second allowed stall on each yields several minutes. Country selection itself is valid and warm revisits are cached, but first-load/restarted-worker globe rendering suffers material delay proportional to the traveller's history, not the promised roughly one-second first render.
findings.evidence: tiles.py:76-89 loops through every intersecting polygon and calls _flag(code) synchronously; :52 makes a blocking request with timeout=20 for each cold flag. Only the completed render is returned/cached at :66-67,107-109; there is no first-stage imagery response or parallel/prefetched flag batch. A read-only bbox calculation against countries50.geojson:1 finds 102 catalogue sovereign codes intersecting z=2,x=2,y=1 (longitude 0..90, latitude 0..66.51), so a traveller with 20 of those visited causes 20 cold flag fetches in one tile.
findings.expected: R-024: "first render completes in roughly a second rather than timing out or returning an error"; checklist, Performance and resource leaks: "Tie a finding to a reachable workload, the mechanism that grows incorrectly and material responsiveness ... loss." Cold rendering must not serialize one external flag download per visited country before any tile can be delivered.
reproduction_steps: Have 20 visited countries in Europe/West Asia intersecting the z=2,x=2,y=1 tile.
Open Mi Mundo after a backend worker restart or otherwise with cold flag/render caches.
Condition: the 20 successful flag-provider replies each take about one second.
The tile renderer waits for them serially before returning any JPEG; repeated requests after completion are cached, but the first globe load is delayed by at least about 20 seconds.

findings.title: Early concurrent Gibraltar saves can persist duplicate visits and stamps — startup accepts writes before the required unique index exists
findings.surface: Fresh deployment startup; POST /api/visited; Gibraltar list/passport/statistics
findings.observed: Data, persistence and APIs: source prediction limited to a fresh database, delayed/failed required index creation and overlapping saves. Startup can accept traffic while the unique visit index is still absent. Two tabs saving Gibraltar can both read no visit and both insert. The subsequent unique-index build then fails on those duplicates and the error is swallowed, so that database stays unprotected. The traveller gets duplicate Gibraltar rows/stamps and a territories_visited count of 2 instead of 1; the sovereign percentage remains set-based. Recovery requires deleting duplicate visits (or operator repair), not a normal reload.
findings.evidence: server.py:942 schedules ensure_indexes() as a background task rather than awaiting it; :944 only awaits storage initialization before startup completes. :68-72 builds indexes sequentially, with the visited_countries unique index declared at :52 after the profiles/trips indexes. :292-294 does a non-atomic find-then-insert. If duplicates arrive first, :73-74 only logs the later unique-index creation failure and continues. stats.py:60,110 counts territory rows rather than a set.
findings.expected: R-006: "Saving Gibraltar again ... does not create a second visit record ... refused by the store"; R-005: "returns exactly one Gibraltar record"; checklist, Data, persistence and APIs: "A check before insert alone races" and "store-enforced uniqueness." The app must not accept visit writes before the uniqueness prerequisite is effective, and a failed required index must not silently leave writes unprotected.
reproduction_steps: Deploy against a fresh database, with storage initialization completing while index creation is still pending (for example a delayed profile-index build).
Before user_country has been built, save Gibraltar for the same account from two overlapping API requests/tabs so both existence checks complete before either insert.
Both inserts can succeed because the store is not yet enforcing uniqueness.
Read /api/visited, /api/passport and /api/stats: duplicate GI rows/stamps and territory count 2 can persist; the later unique-index failure is only logged.

findings_minor.title: Clearing an in-flight city search leaves a permanent spinner — stale-response cleanup never resets the empty-query loading state
findings_minor.surface: CitySearch input in Añadir ciudad, Editar perfil and Explorar
findings_minor.observed: UI state, navigation and interaction: source prediction. Type a query, wait for its request to start, and erase it before the reply. Cleanup invalidates the reply, while the empty-query branch leaves loading true forever. The empty input continues showing the spinner even after the old request completes. The user can still start a new search to recover, so this is minor misleading feedback rather than blocked saving.
findings_minor.evidence: CitySearch.jsx:17 sets loading true when a request starts; :25 marks it stale on input change; :23 then suppresses loading=false for that stale request. The new effect's q.trim().length<2 branch at :14 only clears results and never resets loading or error.
findings_minor.expected: checklist, UI state, navigation and interaction: "Resolve initial, empty, pending, success, failure ... states against the actual operation state" and "failure ending loading." Clearing a city query should clear its loading/error indicators too.
reproduction_steps: In Añadir ciudad, type Roma and wait at least 350 ms for the request to begin.
Before its response arrives, erase the entire query.
Wait for the old request to finish: the spinner is not cleared until another sufficiently long query completes.
